hilt.name: Hilt
hilt.summary: Compile-time dependency injection for Android, built on Dagger. The graph is generated at build time, so a missing binding is a compile error rather than a crash on launch.
hilt.tradeoff: Adds KSP annotation processing to the build.

koin.name: Koin
koin.summary: Pragmatic dependency injection written in pure Kotlin. A small DSL resolves dependencies at runtime, with no annotation processing at all.
koin.tradeoff: Missing bindings surface at runtime, not compile time.

retrofit.name: Retrofit
retrofit.summary: Turns an HTTP API into a Kotlin interface: declare the endpoints, Retrofit writes the calls. Paired here with OkHttp and kotlinx.serialization.

ktor.name: Ktor Client
ktor.summary: Kotlin-first HTTP client, coroutines throughout, with swappable engines. The same code runs on Android, JVM, iOS and JS, so it is the natural pick if you may go multiplatform.
ktor.tradeoff: More manual setup than Retrofit for simple REST calls.

room.name: Room
room.summary: Type-safe SQLite for Android. Your SQL is verified at compile time, and queries return Flows that re-emit whenever the underlying rows change.
room.tradeoff: Adds KSP annotation processing and schema files to version control.

datastore.name: Preferences DataStore
datastore.summary: Asynchronous key-value storage and the modern replacement for SharedPreferences. Reads and writes go through coroutines and Flow, so nothing touches disk on the main thread.
datastore.tradeoff: Key-value only — for relational data you want Room instead. The two are complementary, not alternatives.

none.name: None
none.summary: Leave this layer out. The generated project still compiles and runs — a hand-rolled ServiceLocator replaces the DI framework, and an in-memory repository replaces the database.
none.tradeoff: You can add the real thing later without touching the UI layer, because everything depends on repository interfaces.

sqldelight.name: SQLDelight
sqldelight.summary: Generates typed Kotlin from .sq files, so your SQL is the source of truth rather than annotations on classes. Queries return Flows that re-emit on change.
sqldelight.tradeoff: You write real SQL and it is multiplatform-ready, but there is no Room migration tooling to lean on.

coil.name: Coil
coil.summary: Kotlin-first image loading built on coroutines, with a Compose API (AsyncImage) as a first-class citizen. The de facto choice for Compose projects.

glide.name: Glide
glide.summary: The long-standing Android image loader, battle-tested across huge View-based codebases with strong caching and lifecycle handling.
glide.tradeoff: Its Compose integration is still beta after several years - Coil is the smoother fit for a Compose-only app.
